definition: In this learning-related context, frontal refers to the front part of the brain, especially the midline area where frontal midline theta activity is measured during cognitive processing. Changes in this frontal activity are used as signs of how intensively a person is engaging mental control and effort.

reasons: The packet supports frontal midline theta activity as a measure related to cognitive processing, but it does not define the term “frontal” as the front part of the brain in general.
“Mental control and effort” is not stated in the packet; the source only says frontal midline theta power is a key indicator of cognitive processing and reduced cognitive strain.
The packet does not explicitly define “frontal” as the front part of the brain; it only discusses “frontal midline theta (Fm theta)” without stating that “frontal” refers to the front brain region.

The definition’s claim that changes in frontal activity are “signs of how intensively a person is engaging mental control and effort” is not directly supported; the packet instead links Fm theta power with “cognitive processing” and “cognitive strain,” not explicitly “mental control and effort.”

The packet does support associations between task-related Fm theta power and cognitive processing/cognitive strain, but the definition goes beyond that by specifying the broader “mental control and effort” interpretation.
